_note: MH-21 — the single source of truth for WHICH RAVENCLAUDE COMPONENTS ACTUALLY WORK ON WHICH HOST. Created 2026-07-28 by the multi-host audit. Before this file, every surface that needed the answer either hardcoded it (generate-dashboards.py's _HOOK_CAPABLE_HOSTS) or, more often, silently assumed 'everywhere' — which is how the Pipeline tab came to imply guardrails on hosts that run none, and how Heimdall came to report an unwatched perimeter as clean. A per-component annotation would have been ~20 copies of the same few facts, each free to rot independently; ONE map keeps them honest together.
_contract: `supported` is a claim about whether the component RUNS on that host today, in this repo, as wired by `scripts/ravenclaude`. It is NOT a claim about whether the host is capable in principle — a host can speak a contract perfectly and still be unsupported here because nothing wires it, in which case `supported` is false and `blocked_by` says exactly that. Codex WAS this file's worked example of that distinction until 2026-07-28, when `--host codex` shipped and flipped its hooks + skills cells to true; Cursor is the current example. When a host gains an install path, update this file; do not add a second list somewhere else.
_provenance: verified = confirmed in-repo this session by a visible tool call. docs-verified = read from the host's own documentation this session, url given. inferred = neither; MUST be verified before anything is built on it.

hooks.what: PreToolUse / SessionStart / Stop guardrails — the tribunal, guard-destructive, runaway brake, layout gate, dod gate.

copilot.how: repo-level .github/hooks, wired by `ravenclaude install`, envelope translated by hooks/copilot-hook-adapter.sh
copilot.caveat: PLUGIN-level hooks never fire (github/copilot-cli#2540), which is why they ship repo-level. Tool-name VALUES are lowercase and are normalised in the adapter (f55039ec) — before that fix the tribunal and web guard were silent no-ops.

codex.how: `ravenclaude install --host codex` writes <project>/.codex/hooks.json in the CLAUDE-shaped schema, each entry wrapped through hooks/codex-hook-env.sh. NO envelope adapter: Codex speaks the Claude contract natively (identical PascalCase events, identical stdin fields, identical exit-2 blocking, identical PascalCase tool-name VALUES). The shim's ONLY job is lifting cwd/session_id from the stdin payload into CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/CLAUDE_SESSION_ID, which Codex does not supply.
codex.caveat: HASH-TRUST (MH-17): Codex tracks hook trust by hash, so any change to a hook script marks it for review and SKIPS it until the user re-trusts via /hooks. Because this repo's update model is `git pull`, the steady state for an un-warned user is guardrails silently off after every update — and no banner says so, because the SessionStart banner is itself a hook. The installer and `ravenclaude update` both print the re-trust notice; `requirements.toml` managed hooks are the only unattended-survival configuration.
codex.note: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA ARE supplied by Codex as legacy-compatibility names — an earlier claim in this repo that they were not was wrong and is corrected in knowledge/codex-cli-customization.md. NOTE that _portable.sh's _rc_host_env fallbacks (CODEX_PROJECT_ROOT/SESSION_ID) are speculative names NOT in Codex's documented environment; the shim, not the alias, is what actually closes the gap.
codex.basis: verified 2026-07-28 (installer wires it end-to-end; Gate 155 proves the shim's invariants) + docs-verified (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks)

cursor.how: `ravenclaude install --host cursor` writes <project>/.cursor/hooks.json, PROJECTED from the canonical manifest by scripts/generate-cursor-hooks.py, with each entry wrapped through hooks/cursor-hook-adapter.sh. 20 hooks wired, 5 explicitly skipped with reasons. The enforcing event is beforeShellExecution — the only one whose full input AND output schema Cursor publishes.
cursor.caveat: ⚠ CURSOR FAILS OPEN: a malformed hook response silently ALLOWS the command (Cursor's own bug tracker, verified 2026-07-28) — every other supported host fails CLOSED. The adapter's deny verdict is a fixed literal with no interpolation for exactly this reason. ALSO: the layout gate and web-access guard are NOT enforced here (no verified Cursor event carries a file path pre-write, or an agent web fetch); CI is the backstop and the generated .mdc rules say so. AND: this lane is docs-verified but UNTESTED against a running Cursor — there is no Cursor binary in this repo.
cursor.basis: docs-verified 2026-07-28 (https://cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks) + verified (installer wires it end-to-end; Gates 159/160). NOT verified in a live Cursor session.

skills.what: Agent Skills under .claude/skills — spawn-team, forge, thing, wireframe, and the rest.

codex.how: `ravenclaude install --host codex` symlinks all 50 skills into <project>/.agents/skills/. Codex scans .agents/skills in EVERY directory from cwd up to the repo root, then $HOME/.agents/skills, then /etc/codex/skills, then bundled. SKILL.md needs name+description frontmatter — the same shape as .claude/skills — so the existing skills project across unchanged, with no per-host rewriting.
codex.caveat: NOT `.claude/skills` — that is Copilot's and Claude's read path. Wiring a Codex user there is exactly how `ravenclaude setup` used to complete 'successfully' while wiring zero skills into their host (MH-07).
codex.basis: docs-verified 2026-07-28 (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/build-skills) + verified (installer wires it; 50 skills confirmed in a scratch install). NOTE: multiple third-party guides claim `.codex/skills`; the primary source says `.agents/skills`. Trust this row, not a blog.

instruction_files.what: Does the host automatically read AGENTS.md (the cross-tool discipline)?

copilot.how: reads AGENTS.md natively, but only from the USER's repo — `ravenclaude install` now writes .github/copilot-instructions.md pointing at the projected copy (3486637e)

codex.how: reads AGENTS.md from the repo root

cursor.how: `ravenclaude install --host cursor` writes .cursor/rules/*.mdc — Cursor's OWN convention, which its docs describe as the scoped alternative to AGENTS.md rather than a superset. Two rules: an always-on discipline pointer, and a glob-scoped layout-allow-list rule (MH-25).
cursor.caveat: AGENTS.md auto-load by Cursor remains unconfirmed; the .mdc rules are what this repo actually wires, so do not rely on AGENTS.md reaching a Cursor session on its own.

gemini.blocked_by: reads GEMINI.md; this repo provides none

aider.blocked_by: Aider documents CONVENTIONS.md, loaded ONLY on explicit opt-in (--read / .aider.conf.yml). AGENTS.md is not mentioned in its docs at all. AGENTS.md:3 previously claimed otherwise; corrected in a5d7e4bf.

windsurf.blocked_by: unverified, and the product was reportedly renamed to Devin Desktop (2026-06-02)
